Rachel —

Appreciate the materials. Quick read-through and a couple clarifying points from our side (procurement looped in):

1) Reseller margin floor: Acme's procurement indicated any floor needs to be vendor-backed for the first 12 months and include an audit clause. Is Redwood comfortable providing an "audit-and-true-up" for year 1 only?
2) Step-up visibility: Acme wants predictable annual increases with maximum % stated in the offer (they don't want ad-hoc bumps). Can Redwood commit to a maximum annual step of 5%? If so, procurement will be more comfortable.
3) Pass-through fees: Atlas asks that any marketplace pass-through or listing fees be clearly called out and excluded from the margin calculation.

Also, procurement asked whether you can provide a sample redline on standard private-offer T&Cs (esp. commit definitions, true-up timing). If you can send a marked-up terms doc, we can run it through Acme legal faster.

Happy to jump on a call Wed/Thu.

Rachel / Laura —

Read Maria's questions and drafted recommended concessions to move the deal forward while protecting Redwood economics:

Summary of proposed changes to propose back to Atlas/Acme:
- Reseller margin floor: Agree to an 18% floor with an audit-and-true-up clause limited to the first 12 months. If audit shows shortfall, Redwood will credit the difference in the next invoice period (no retroactive cash refunds).
- Annual step-ups: Commit to maximum annual list-price increase of 5%. We'll bake the exact annual % into the private-offer matrix so increases are deterministic (Scenario B: 3% Y2, 4% Y3).
- Pass-through fees: Explicitly exclude marketplace listing fees and any third-party pass-throughs from the margin calculation. We'll add an appendix listing known fees and how they're treated.
- Commit definition: Use consumption-based commit with monthly true-up; anything within the committed band is considered satisfied. For overages, standard overage rates apply (we'll keep them consistent with the public pricing floor).

Attached my redline: redline_terms.docx — it highlights the audit mechanics, true-up timing, and reseller margin calculation table. If Rachel signs off, I can convert to a PDF and send to Maria + procurement.

Impact note: Under Scenario B (3%/4%) Redwood's NPV on the commit improves ~2.1% vs Scenario A (flat price) while the partner still sees a ~1.4% uplift in netback over the three-year period due to protected commission bands.

If we want to be more aggressive, we could offer a limited early-adopter credit in Y1 (one-time invoice credit) rather than increasing the list price in Y2–Y3, but that reduces binding economics for Redwood. Recommend the 18% floor + deterministic step-ups approach.

Ben
